blocks.text: Arabian Concern of Infrastructure and Logistic is an international construction and transport concern. ACIL was a small startup from the Arabian Peninsula, which signed a contract with [[crust|CRUST]] for transportation of materials for a space elevator and preparation of a construction site. ACIL actively cooperates with other corporations on cargo transportation, and after the beginning of lunar exploration the concern signed a new contract with Crust for creation of lunar infrastructure.

ai-center.summary: Passively processes data for research, accelerating the discovery process.

gameText.heading: AI Center
paragraphs: AI Center is a computational hub capable of processing and structuring massive volumes of scientific data. It hosts a specialized neural network adapted to the lunar environment and colonization tasks. This module is what opens the path to technological breakthroughs for the colonists by generating additional research points.

The AI Center automatically forms hypotheses, simulates experiments, cross-checks results with available archives, and thereby accelerates the process of scientific discovery. Its operation requires a constant power supply and stable data input.

blocks.text: "Argos" is a complex of automated research stations and satellites controlled by artificial intelligence orbiting Io, a satellite of Jupiter. The Argos project was established in 2075 as part of the Galileo Network research initiative. Io's constant volcanic activity and extreme radiation levels prevented the establishment of a permanent colony on the satellite, so its exploration was entrusted to the experimental artificial intelligence "Argos". "Argos" became a decentralized Al whose copies were placed in orbiting satellites and connected via laser communication technology. 'Argos manages research modules and drones on Io and conducts surveillance from orbit.

gameText.heading: Assembler
paragraphs: Assembler — a flexible production module offering alternative recipes for manufacturing materials and components.

Assemblers trace their origins to adaptive robo-workshops that were actively used during natural disasters and military operations of the 21st century. Their popularity surged during the global resource shortages when supply chains collapsed and companies needed universal solutions.
Within the CRUST lunar program, assemblers became indispensable: they enabled rapid production reconfiguration without the need to redesign entire complexes.

gameText.heading: Carbon Fiber Factory
paragraphs: Carbon Fiber Factory is a high-tech industrial facility designed to synthesize carbon fiber from organic materials and water. Carbon fiber is a strong, lightweight structural material that is critical for assembling complex machinery.

The module uses automated chemical reactors and nanostructuring extrusion systems. During the process, organics undergo thermal decomposition and catalytic treatment, forming long carbon chains. gameText.heading: Cargo Dock
paragraphs: Cargo Dock — this is a ground transport terminal where loading and unloading of cargo lunar rovers take place. The dock is equipped with containers for loose materials and pallets for solid cargo, as well as conveyor outputs for efficient task execution.

blocks.text: The Cargo Dock is a ground transport terminal for loading and unloading cargo trucks. It is equipped with containers for bulk and pallets for solid cargo, along with conveyor exits for rapid task execution.
Robotic manipulators and powerful electromagnets allow for quick loading and unloading of heavy cargo without requiring operator involvement.
Cargo docks have been widely used in industrial and mining enterprises on the lunar surface since its full-scale development.
The **Cargo Dock** has 6 programmable output conveyor ports: 4 on one side and 2 on the opposite side.
Drones do not appear to take from the Cargo Dock so this is the only way to removed items delivered to the cargo dock.

The **Cargo Dock** is usually placed on the surface near a [[conveyor-elevator|Conveyor Elevator]] so that bulk items received from [[mobile-drilling-rig|Mobile Drilling Rig]]s or other mining vehcile can be transported underground for processing.

gameText.heading: Conveyor Lift
paragraphs: Conveyor Lift is designed for the vertical transportation of resources and materials. Such lifts serve as connecting links in the overall conveyor system, optimizing logistical flows and speeding up the transport of goods from extraction and processing sites to loading terminals.

The lift includes a conveyor belt equipped with buckets and corrugated edges to prevent spillage or tipping of the transported cargo, as well as a reinforced support structure capable of handling large volumes of heavy materials.

Conveyor lifts were first introduced in the mid-2070s when underground extractors began replacing surface ones. Initially, a general cargo lift was used for material transport, but the need for process automation in mass mining soon became apparent.

blocks.text: The **Conveyor Elevator** is a logistics module that coveys resources between the surface and underground. This is useful for both moving resources brought in from outside the base underground to the factory an for moving finished goods from the underground factory to the transportation infrastructure to fulfill contracts.
There is no speed modifier for the **Conveyor Elevator**. It will match the highest speed of any attached conveyor. Drones do not take from or deliver to the **Conveyor Elevator**.
The **Conveyor Elevator** has 4 configurable bidirectional conveyor ports at the top and 4 at the bottom.
It has storage for the following resources.

Locating the **Conveyor Elevator** requires making sure that it is placed on a suitable position both on the surface and underground. The Game Interface will display a smaller window showing the opposite surface to allow better control of placement.
The ghost module will be red when the **Conveyor Elevator** is in an invalid location and will turn blue when the module is in a valid location.

It is a good idea to position a **Conveyor Elevator** near a [[cargo-dock|Cargo Dock]]] on the surface so that [[regolith|Regolith]] and [[rare-earth-minerals|Rare Earth Minerals]] (and later various oxides) can be transported quickly to where they are needed. Placing a [[large-bulk-storage|Large Bulk Storage]] module for each resource near the underground side of the same elevator will allow the Cargo Cock to be emptied facter so it does not backlog deliveries.
There are no upgrades available for the **Conveyor Elevator**.

gameText.heading: Conveyor
paragraphs: Conveyor — a belt-driven transport device that moves bulk, lumpy, or individual goods automatically. The conveyor belt system significantly accelerates the transportation of cargo from extraction sites to production facilities, thereby increasing processing efficiency and product output.

A belt conveyor consists of several key components: drive drum, conveyor drive, tension drum, tensioning unit, load-bearing belt section, support rollers, and a conveyor frame made of welded metal profiles. Modern conveyors feature a modular design, allowing the conveyor line length to be adjusted as needed.
Upgraded conveyor systems transport goods significantly faster than basic models, providing more efficient logistics.

gameText.heading: Underground Conveyor
paragraphs: Underground Conveyor performs the same functions as a regular conveyor but has a number of structural differences. Underground conveyors are placed in small yet durable metal pipes reinforced with stiffening ribs to enhance structural strength. These pipes protect the conveyor belts and transported cargo from cave-ins or collapses of rock above the conveyor line. The pipe restricts the underground conveyor to a straight line, but it also allows conveyors to be installed at varying depths to prevent belt intersections.

Underground Conveyor is a more expensive but more efficient version of standard conveyors that frees up surface space for constructing additional modules. Underground conveyors help make the production complex more compact and optimize the entire conveyor system.

blocks.text: This research increases the amount of money returned when deconstructing a conveyor to 100% of it's build cost.
**Programmable Splitter**: 6,000 / 600 / 1,100 points (branches not stated on the wiki) Note: currently WIP.
To build conveyor belts open the conveyor belt menu.
Here you can select the elemnts you want to build as well as a selection to upgrade or dismantle existing conveyors. You also have a selection to make belts drop the items that are currently on them.

"Building" a conveyor in this mode doesn't actually place them or spend any resources. Instead a "ghost" is placed. This allows you to plan massive conveyor networks, even if you don't have the resources to actually build them.
Hovering over one of these ghosts will highlight a segment. Holding "Alt" (default) and clicking on it will build the highlighted section, spending the required resources.

Hovering over one of these ghosts while pressing "Shift" (default) and having either the "Upgrade" or "Dismantle" tool active will highlight all directly connected sections, allowing you to mass upgrade or dismantle entire conveyor sections.

When merging or splitting conveyors a Distributor is automatically planned at the intersection. This automatically built Distributor is not to be confused with the Programmable Splitter, though it does have a basic filter system. The automatically generated version cannot be manually created.

When no filters are applied, the distributor works in a soft round-robin mode: It will send one item to each output, then start again from the first. If an output that would receive an item next is blocked (either by a setting, the output not having a conveyor connected or the connected conveyor being full or saturated) it is simply skipped.
The standard distributor has (when selected) a basic filter system for every output. The 5 buttons are (left-to-right): Priority output, Reset settings, Manual control, Block output, Resources.

If the priority output is set then the distributor will first check this output. If it is not blocked it will send the incoming resource to this output. If multiple outputs are set as priority output it will operate with the same soft round-robin logic it uses during normal operation with everything besides the priority outputs being treated like blocked. Only after an item was unable to be sent to any priority output it will enter the distribution logic for the non-priority outputs.
The ”Reset Settings” button resets all output settings to the default values, those being non-priority, unblocked and no resource filter.
The “Block output” toggle blocks the distributor from outputting any items to this output.

With the resources submenu you are able to set resource filters for this specific output. Items that are not on this filter will never be output here. Items that cannot be output to any side will instead block the distributor.
There are currently no input-side settings for the distributor
The Programmable Splitter is currently marked as work in progress.

The underground conveyor belt does not impose a speed limit of its own, instead using the lower speed of whatever conveyor tiers are connected to its respective input and output side. The limitation that is lifted with research is it's range instead. It's default range is able to bridge 7 tiles. The advanced researches increase this limit by the following values (additive):
At max research an underground connection can bridge 27 cells.

If a conveyor section is connected directly to a machine or storage input hatch it seems to only accept items that it would be able to input into said input hatch. This behaviour requires further testing.
Conveyors can be brought to the other layer using the [[conveyor-elevator|Conveyor elevator]]. It will not see further discussion in this context.

expedition-control-center.summary: The Expedition Control Center coordinates research missions outside the base. It ensures communication with research groups, allowing the dispatch of transport vehicles with drones or colonists to remote lunar locations.

gameText.heading: Expedition Center
paragraphs: Expedition Center coordinates research missions outside the base. It provides communication with research teams and allows the dispatch of transport rovers with drones or colonists to remote locations on the Moon.

To maintain communication with objects on the Moon, the Expedition Center is equipped with a large array of radio equipment for data transmission, as well as numerous servers and computers for processing received information. Modern equipment enables route planning, monitoring, data analysis, and operational decision-making in fully automated mode.

After lunar exploration began in the 2060s, the need to change the approach to studying its surface became apparent. The distance to command centers on Earth made real-time equipment control inefficient, and control stations at the "Hope-1" station quickly became overwhelmed with tasks. In 2069, SCT Ltd. and FASM introduced a prototype expedition management module that required operator involvement. In 2074, SCT Ltd., in collaboration with NERPA, presented a project for an automated expedition control center, which became the foundation for all subsequent models.

gameText.heading: Regolith Extractor
paragraphs: Regolith Extractor — this is a universal mining module designed for extracting resource-rich regolith from underground deposits. The extractor uses a descending drill to break up lunar rock and create a borehole. A system of pipes and compressors lifts the crushed and ground rock, preparing it for further processing. The drills of extractors are highly durable, allowing them to handle most types of rock.

The prototype of a stationary drilling rig for lunar use was developed in 2059 as part of the "First Step" project, which aimed to lay the groundwork for further satellite exploration. The Malachite Concern played a key role in its development, applying its extensive experience in the production and application of mining equipment. Mass production of extractors began in the late 2060s.

blocks.text: The Regolith Extractor is a versatile mining module designed for extracting resource-rich regolith from underground deposits.

The extractor uses a descending drill to break lunar rock and create a borehole. With the help of a system of pipes and compressors, the crushed and pulverized rock is raised and prepared for further technological processes. The drills of the extractors have increased strength, allowing them to work with most types of rock.

The prototype of the stationary drilling rig for use on the Moon was developed in 2059 as part of the "First Step" project, which aimed to lay the foundation for further exploration of the satellite. The "Malachite" consortium played a key role in the development, leveraging their experience in the production and use of mining equipment. Mass production of extractors began in the late 2060s.

gameText.heading: Mission Control Center, MCC
paragraphs: Mission Control Center, MCC is a facility designed to manage orbital logistics, cargo dispatch, and reception. The MCC is equipped with a landing pad for incoming transport capsules and conveyor outputs for efficient loading and unloading of goods. Additionally, it grants access to upgraded capsules with increased capacity and speed.
MCC combines the roles of a landing platform, cargo terminal, and control hub.

This versatility proved extremely useful on the Moon, leading to the widespread adoption of standardized MCCs starting in the early 2070s. The design of modern MCCs originated from the engineering division of UNIVERSE, which developed the prototype under the “Program for the Unification and Standardization of Flight Regulations in Near-Earth and Space Environments” in 2072. As part of the UN, UNIVERSE released the MCC production license, making all design documentation publicly available and free to use.

blocks.text: The Flight Control Center, FCC, is a facility designed for managing orbital logistics, sending, and receiving cargo. The FCC is equipped with a landing platform for transport capsules and conveyor exits for efficient loading and unloading of goods.

The FCC combines the roles of a landing platform, cargo terminal, and control hub. This versatility proved extremely useful on the Moon, leading to the widespread use of standardized FCCs from the early 2070s. The modern FCC models were developed by the design department of UNIVERSE as part of the “Program for Unification and Standardization of Flight Regulations in Near-Earth and Space Environments” in 2072. As a UN entity, UNIVERSE licensed the production of FCCs, and all design documentation became publicly accessible and free to use.

"Khandir is the most distant inhabited object in the solar system. It was founded by Crust in 2089 as part of a project to create a transshipment base for exploring distant planets and satellites. gameText.heading: Landing Platform
paragraphs: Landing Platform is a specialized pad for preparing cargo capsules for launch. These platforms simplify cargo operations, and according to CRUST regulations, a landing platform or its equivalent is required to fulfill commercial contracts.

Concrete blocks are used for the platform's foundation, while the frame and body are constructed from steel. The platform is equipped with a signal beacon for nighttime navigation, and special markings are applied to its surface.

Developed in 2076 by the construction conglomerate ACIL, the Landing Platform significantly reduced the risk of accidents during cargo capsule landings. This became especially important after the widespread adoption of low-cost transport capsule models with reduced durability.

gameText.heading: Microchip Factory
paragraphs: Microchip Factory produces microelectronic circuits for advanced industrial equipment. The module is equipped for the full cycle of microelectronics production, from design to photolithography, assembly, and testing. Complex algorithms and high-tech equipment allow all operations to be carried out automatically, without the need for personnel.

The pioneer of microchip and microcircuit production on the Moon was the HEMISCO corporation. As a near-monopoly in the terrestrial microelectronics market, the company moved to occupy the lunar manufacturing niche in 2073, when the first major factory was opened on the satellite. Eventually, competitors began actively designing and constructing their own compact production complexes, ending HEMISCO’s monopoly. The tech race concluded in 2079 with the release of a licensed model of the automated microchip factory.

blocks.text: "Minos" is an international research station on Europa, a satellite of Jupiter. The space program to establish a base on Europa was developed by [[crust|CRUST]] in 2071. The colony was erected in 2076 based on an existing automated outpost from the Galileo Grid project, and the transportation of cargo and colonists was provided by the XSpace Corporation. "Minos" is a research base hidden beneath a column of ice to protect it from radiation. It is home to about two hundred scientists and colonists who are engaged in a comprehensive study of the satellite's surface and its underground ocean. The colony is gradually expanding and constructing new facilities in the ice as necessary materials are delivered from Earth, the Moon, and Mars.

gameText.heading: Modular Terminals Factory
paragraphs: Modular Terminals Factory assembles universal user interfaces used in automation, life support systems, and human-machine interaction. Modular terminals are essential for configuring and controlling lunar base equipment, as well as for communication between various modules and AI systems.

The production process includes several stages: casing assembly, installation of sensory and tactile interfaces, and integration of all components into a single functional block. The components provide a reliable mechanical framework, while the microcircuits form the computational core of the terminals. All stages are automated and take place in a sterile assembly environment.

blocks.text: The Multi-Regolith Refinery is an advanced version of the Single Regolith Refinery, designed to extract multiple types of oxides from lunar regolith. This module crushes the rock and separates oxides from slag using a chemical decomposition procedure.

gameText.heading: Ore Detector
paragraphs: Ore Detector — this is an electromagnetic spectrometer that allows detection of mineral deposits and identification of their chemical composition.

blocks.text: Ore Detector — this is an electromagnetic spectrometer that allows detection of mineral deposits and identification of their chemical composition.
To locate ore-rich regolith deposits, select a built ore detector, wait for it to charge, and designate an area for scanning.
Using the Detector consumes electricity. The larger the scanning area, the more energy is required.

The spectrometer's operating principle is based on measuring electromagnetic radiation that is reflected, scattered, or absorbed with varying intensity depending on the element or compound. The spectrometer'a sensors are highly sensitive and very fragile, so operating rules prohibit placing scanners on surfaces where regolith dust and solar radiation can damage them.

Multispectral scanning of the Moon was conducted out even before the construction of the space elevator using spectrometers on satellites and observatories, but only after the industrial development of the satellite began was it possible to scan the surface with devices directly at mining sites. Detectors from the HEMISCO Corporation became the first mass-produced items on the market, enabling the start of the lunar mining industry in the mid-2060s.
Requires the Regolith Pressing research to unlock.

pressing-module.title: Pressing Module
pressing-module.summary: Inefficient production of Smart Concrete from Regolith.

gameText.heading: Pressing Machine
paragraphs: Pressing Machine — this is a module for producing smart concrete using high-temperature vibropressing technology. The raw material for concrete production is unrefined lunar soil, which causes valuable mineral elements to become part of the concrete alongside slag.

The resulting mixture is thoroughly mixed to a uniform consistency before being placed into molds for future blocks. The mixture in the molds is then heated, and high-frequency vibration pressing begins. The vibrations create mechanical oscillations in the materials, aiding in the compression and compaction of the regolith within the mold. This process allows for the rapid production of durable construction material suitable for use on the Moon and Earth. This technology was developed and certified by CRUST in 2057 with ACIL's participation as part of the "First Step" project.

blocks.text: The Pressing Module is a unit for producing Smart Concrete using high-temperature vibrocompression technology. The raw material for making concrete is unrefined lunar soil, which means that useful mineral elements become part of the concrete along with the slag.

The mixture obtained is thoroughly mixed until a uniform consistency is achieved, then placed into molds for the future blocks. The mixture in the molds is then heated and simultaneously pressed with high-frequency vibration. The vibrations create mechanical oscillations in the materials, which contribute to the compression and densification of the regolith inside the mold. This treatment allows for the quick production of a durable building material suitable for use on both the Moon and Earth.
This technology was developed and certified by CRUST in 2057 with the participation of ACIL as part of the "First Step" project.
The **Pressing Module** has one input connection for Regolith with a buffer of 128 and one output connection for Smart Concrete with a buffer size of 32.

blocks.text: Extracted from underground with the [[extractor|Regolith Extractor]] or on the surface of the moon via the [[mobile-drilling-rig|Mobile Drilling Rig]]. Regolith can be refined into oxides by using the [[single-regolith-refinery|Single Regolith Refinery]] or the [[multi-regolith-refinery|Multi-Regolith Refinery]]

When mined Regolith will have a certain amount of richness for each of the oxides and [[slag|Slag]]. When underground, you can determine the richness by the type of ore node you place [[extractor|Regolith Extractor]] on. On the surface you can scan for different oxide types with the [[rover-scout|Rover Scout]]'s Geological Scanner. If regolith of different richnesses is combined the resulting richness is the weighted average of the input regoliths.

The richness average of [[extractor|Regolith Extractors]] placed on underground ore deposits is 20% [[silicon-oxide|Silicon Oxide]], 20% [[titanium-oxide|Titanium Oxide]], 20% [[iron-oxide|Iron Oxide]], 20% [[aluminum-oxide|Aluminum Oxide]], and 20% [[slag|Slag]].

The Richness is used to determine the amount of a given element that is gained from regolith generated from this particular source. In the above example, a single regolith refinery set to process silicon oxide would create approximately 1.6 [[silicon-oxide|Silicon Oxide]] and 6 [[slag|Slag]] for every 20 [[regolith|Regolith]].

gameText.heading: Single Regolith Refinery
paragraphs: Single Regolith Refinery is designed to extract oxides from lunar regolith. The module's construction allows the refinery to be built with minimal material costs, but limits its functionality. Extracting oxides requires specialized reagents and precise equipment tuning, so refineries are capable of processing only one type of oxide at a time.

The refinery operates by isolating valuable elements from lunar soil, or regolith. To do this, regolith is ground down and enters into thermochemical reactions with various substances and compounds. The resulting oxides are separated from slag using separators and sent for further processing.

Regolith refineries began to be used on the Moon at the start of industrial mineral extraction. Originally developed by the Malachite corporation, this system continues to play a key role in lunar manufacturing.

In the refinery units, the regolith is crushed and undergoes thermochemical interaction with other substances and compounds. paragraphs: Smelting Furnace uses high-temperature melting to process oxides into blanks for further production.

paragraphs: Online Market — an electronic platform for trade between organizations on the Moon. Access to the market allows you to purchase missing materials for production or convert surplus resources into money.

Market prices are formed dynamically, based on current supply and demand: the more of a certain type of resource you put on the market, the lower its price will be. A Landing Platform is required to send resources to the market.
Trading on the online market helps optimize resource and financial management, ensuring sustainable development of a lunar enterprise.

blocks.text: I have a solution to our problems, Director. We can establish trade with other organizations on the Moon. This way, surplus resources are converted into money, which we currently lack. To send resources, we need a Landing Platform, and to access the market, we need to research the Online Market.
Research it under Social, then build a [[landing-platform|Landing Platform]]. Everything is ready for trading. You can now sell your excess resources on the “Online Market” in the Control Center.

items: **Sell price** is the market’s current price, rounded down.
**Buy price** is the current price times a markup that differs by resource (×1.1 to ×1.4 in the data read so far).
Each resource has a **base price** and can only move inside a band around it, for example ×0.5 to ×1.5 for Smart Concrete and ×0.82 to ×1.18 for Quantum Computers.
**Supply** is compared with a normal market volume. Resources well below normal volume sell above base; well above normal, below base.
The market keeps a **30-day price history** for each resource.

blocks.text: _These price rules were read from the running 1.0.6.1 game by CrustWatcher, not from a published formula._

items: Selling adds supply, so a large sale gets a lower average price than the quoted one. Split big sales when the price is near its 30-day high.
Shipments go by capsule and have a transport cost; see [[contracts-and-tenders|contracts]] for why the AI Analyst’s estimates leave it out.
Your reputation affects market prices; see [[bank-and-reputation|Bank and reputation]].
With [[auto-trading|auto-trading]], visiting ships buy and sell for you when your price is competitive.

blocks.text: The Crust left Early Access on **2026-09-10**. Your game reports version **1.0.6.1**, the newest build as of 2026-09-12.

items: **Planning Mode.** Planning Mode allows you to design a construction plan for modules and the conveyor network, and also displays a counter for the resources and credits required to execute the plan.

construction-costs.title: Construction costs
construction-costs.summary: Building spends credits, including conveyors and wires, and counts toward capitalization.

blocks.text: Modules cost resources to build and credits to place; conveyors and electrical wires cost credits too. Everything you build counts toward [[capitalization|capitalization]].

items: Demolishing refunds part of the cost; the [[conveyor-belts|Complete recycling of conveyors and wires]] research raises conveyor refunds to 100%.
Since hotfix 1.0.6, removing roads with the Universal Demolition tool refunds their credits correctly.
Planning Mode allows you to design a construction plan for modules and the conveyor network, and also displays a counter for the resources and credits required to execute the plan.
